newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico same-day peso ends weaker on falling stocks.
newsitem.headline: Mexico same-day peso ends weaker on falling stocks.

text.p: Mexico's same-day peso closed six centavos weaker at 7.5630/7.5670 per dollar on a falling stock market and rising bond yields in the United States but off the day's lows.

"The peso fell very quickly, and we had the misfortune that the yield on the U.S. long-bond rose as well," one dealer said. "But the market is a little less nervous and the peso started to rebound...."
In early trade the same day peso contract weakened 11.3 centavos before recovering.
The 24-hour peso was trading 5.7 centavos weaker at 7.575/7.58 per dollar, while the spot 48-hour was 4.75 centavos weaker at 7.5825/7.5875 per dollar.
The stock market was down almost 2.0 percent in mid-day trade.
Mexican markets were also being affected by political uncertainty tied to guerrilla attacks in two southern states this week.
"A lot had to do with speculation and nervousness about the guerrillas, but also to do with the instability of the (U.S.) long bond," said one dealer.
The U.S. long-bond was yielding 7.12 percent.
